name: CA-41
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's nine-point Democratic partisan lean favors the incumbent party
Overwhelming fundraising gap: Sanchez has $1.9 million raised versus under $6,000 for Clemmons
Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Sanchez near 96 percent
No public polling or expert ratings signal any competitive risk
model.rationale: A nine-point Democratic district, a fundraising advantage of roughly three hundred to one, and prediction markets near 96 percent all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting any threat to the incumbent.
model.watch: Clemmons has no visible campaign resources, so only a late outside-spending surge or an unexpected scandal involving Sanchez would put the seat in question.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Linda Sanchez, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a district whose recent partisan lean favors her party by nine points. No independent public polls cover the general election, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, campaign resources and market pricing. Both Kalshi and Polymarket price Sanchez's chances near 96 percent.

The fundraising gap is stark: Sanchez has raised about $1.9 million and holds roughly $462,000 on hand, while Republican Mitch Clemmons has raised under $6,000 with about $4,000 available. No outside spending has been reported against the incumbent, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Every available indicator points to a comfortable win for Sanchez, with the open question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
